title: Fair Work Amendment (Right to Work from Home) Bill 2025
short_title: Fair Work Amendment (Right to Work from Home) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would expand employees' access to flexible work requests and establish a specific right to ask to work from home up to two days weekly.
Employers could refuse these home-working requests only where the arrangement would make the job's inherent requirements impractical or impossible, rather than relying on broader business grounds.
The changes would apply prospectively, with the substantive schedule starting the day after Royal Assent and the Fair Work Commission able to resolve disputes.
changes: Eligibility limits based on particular caring, disability or age-related circumstances would be removed.
Employers would have to explore reasonable adjustments before refusing a request for up to two home-working days.
Employers would need to genuinely engage with employees about requests.
The Fair Work Commission could make binding decisions on whether refusals meet the statutory test.
summary.affected: Employees seeking flexible working arrangements, their employers and the Fair Work Commission are affected.
